label: Week 37, 2026
recap:
This was a quiet week for United States AI policy, with three bill movements recorded and no case updates or federal documents. Activity was concentrated in the United States Congress, which accounted for two of the tracked jurisdictions worth of activity, alongside one bill movement in Pennsylvania. In total, two jurisdictions saw any change in status.

The main thread running through the week was infrastructure and energy, with two bills touching on data centers, the power they draw, and the local cost of hosting them, including Pennsylvania HB2760. There was also a single bill movement on children and minors, with United States Congress HB10315 addressing companion chatbots, age verification, school use, and protections for people under eighteen. No other themes appeared in the data this week.

reading.body:
No bills moved, no cases advanced, and no federal documents were recorded in US AI policy between September 7 and 13, 2026.

The week produced no measurable activity across any tracked category: legislation, litigation, or federal agency action. This absence could reflect genuine lull, gaps in data collection, or the summer-fall transition typical in policy cycles. Without positive indicators of movement, the record shows only silence.

The lack of activity means nothing can be inferred about regulatory momentum, court precedent, or agency priorities during this period. This data documents what did not happen rather than what did.
